title: When the Cover Breaks
premise: Emrys Sandoval has spent a decade laundering the reputations of the powerful, tracing dirty money until it comes out clean and unattributable—work so sensitive her own name barely exists. When a burner phone arrives with no sender and rings with the voice of her presumed-dead mentor, Ilya Voss, she is pulled into a plot to destroy the Meridian Summit using a financial weapon disguised as an infrastructure accident. Following money trails that lead into her own buried past, Emrys discovers the attack is funded by the very firm that erased her identity—and that Ilya faked his death to stop them from inside. In the end, Emrys chooses exposure over invisibility, breaking the cover on both the conspiracy and herself, saving the summit and finally belonging to the found family of colleagues and strangers who refuse to let her disappear.
about_author: Casper Eastwick is a former compliance analyst who spent years watching money move in ways no one wanted explained, and now writes thrillers about the people who watch back. Eastwick lives quietly off the grid, which is easier to do in fiction than in fact.

chapters.title: Clean Money
chapters.summary: Emrys closes another unattributable case for Halcyon Risk Group, erasing a senator's laundering trail, and returns to a bare apartment that reflects how thoroughly she's erased herself. POV: Emrys. Beat: competent isolation—the comfort and cost of invisibility established.

chapters.title: The Phone That Shouldn't Ring
chapters.summary: A padded envelope with no return address contains a burner phone. At 3 a.m. it rings: Ilya Voss, her mentor who died in a ferry fire two years ago, tells her to pull the Meridian Summit's infrastructure financing before the 'accident.' POV: Emrys. Beat: vertigo—the past refusing to stay buried.

chapters.title: Ghost Protocol
chapters.summary: Emrys verifies the voice against old case files and finds the ferry fire's insurance payout routed through a shell company she herself once sanitized. She realizes her own work may be stitched into the plot. POV: Emrys. Beat: guilt and dread—her clean money isn't clean.

chapters.title: Dara
chapters.summary: Emrys recruits Dara Okafor, a disgraced journalist and the closest thing she has to a friend, breaking her own rule about involving others. Dara agrees, sensing Emrys is finally letting someone in. POV: alternating Emrys and Dara. Beat: fragile trust—the first thread of found family.

chapters.title: Meridian
chapters.summary: Emrys infiltrates a Summit pre-conference under a borrowed identity and maps the financing web: a port expansion project whose collapse would kill hundreds and crater three currencies. POV: Emrys. Beat: rising stakes—the attack has a shape and a clock.

chapters.title: The Handler's Smile
chapters.summary: Halcyon assigns Emrys a new handler, Corin Vale, whose friendly questions feel like tests. She realizes Halcyon may already suspect she's off-script—and that Vale's charm is surveillance. POV: Emrys. Beat: paranoia—the institution that owns her identity tightens its grip.

chapters.title: Burner Conversations
chapters.summary: Ilya feeds Emrys fragments: a name, 'Kestrel,' and a warning that Halcyon built the attack's cover. He refuses to meet, and Emrys confronts her grief and anger at a man who let her mourn him. POV: Emrys, with flashback to her training under Ilya. Beat: betrayal braided with loyalty.

chapters.title: Kestrel
chapters.summary: Dara's digging identifies Kestrel as a Halcyon board seat held in trust—an entity Emrys recognizes as the one that funded her own identity erasure. Her past and the plot share a spine. POV: Emrys. Beat: the personal becomes the case; identity as both wound and weapon.

chapters.title: Safehouse Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Hunted after accessing Halcyon archives, Emrys and Dara hide in a shuttered laundromat owned by Tomas Reyes, a retired analyst who once worked with Ilya and owes him a life. Tomas joins them. POV: Dara. Beat: the found family takes shape over cheap coffee and shared danger.

chapters.title: What Vale Knows
chapters.summary: Vale corners Emrys at a gallery fundraiser, revealing he knows about the phone and offering her a deal: deliver Ilya, keep her cover. She realizes Vale isn't Halcyon's loyalist—he's Kestrel's enforcer. POV: Emrys. Beat: temptation and threat in one silk-wrapped package.

chapters.title: The Ferry File
chapters.summary: Tomas decrypts the real ferry-fire report: Ilya staged his death to infiltrate Kestrel after discovering the Summit plot, sacrificing his name the way Emrys once sacrificed hers. POV: Emrys with Tomas. Beat: grief reframed—Ilya's 'betrayal' was a mirror of her own life.

chapters.title: Ledger of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Emrys reconstructs Kestrel's funding chain and finds the trigger mechanism: a derivatives position that pays out only if the port fails on summit day. The attack is an arbitrage. POV: Emrys. Beat: cold clarity—the horror is bureaucratic, and that's what makes it terrifying.

chapters.title: Compromised
chapters.summary: Halcyon burns Dara's career, leaking fabricated stories to isolate her, and Vale freezes Emrys's accounts and identities. Stripped of every cover, the two are left with only each other. POV: Dara. Beat: loss and resolve—belonging forged by being unmade together.

chapters.title: Dead Drop at the Fish Market
chapters.summary: Following Ilya's instructions, Emrys attempts a meet; it's ambushed by Vale's team. Ilya saves her, and they finally stand face to face—older, angrier, alive. POV: Emrys. Beat: catharsis and confrontation; the reunion is not a comfort but a reckoning.

chapters.title: Confessions in a Stolen Car
chapters.summary: Ilya explains Kestrel's endgame: collapse the port, trigger the derivatives, buy the wreckage, and remake the region's economy under Halcyon's thumb—with Emrys's old sanitization work as the laundering backbone. He asks her to finish it. POV: Ilya. Beat: the mentor's guilt meets the student's choice.

chapters.title: The Vote
chapters.summary: The team debates: expose everything publicly and risk Halcyon burying it, or feed the evidence to a single trustworthy regulator and risk a leak. Emrys, for the first time, lets others decide with her. POV: alternating. Beat: democracy inside the found family; Emrys stops operating alone.

chapters.title: Into the Machine
chapters.summary: Emrys goes back inside Halcyon, wearing Vale's offered deal as camouflage, to plant a tripwire in the derivatives settlement code that will expose the payout the moment it triggers. POV: Emrys. Beat: the invisible woman weaponizes her own erasure.

chapters.title: Vale's Ledger
chapters.summary: Vale catches the tripwire and confronts Emrys with her entire fabricated history, offering to restore her real name in exchange for Ilya. She realizes her 'real' identity was itself a Halcyon construction. POV: Emrys. Beat: identity collapses—there was never a cover to return to.

chapters.title: Summit Eve
chapters.summary: With hours left, Kestrel accelerates the timeline; Tomas is captured buying equipment, and Dara's last source goes silent. The team is broken, the clock is merciless. POV: Dara. Beat: darkest hour—everything the found family built is being torn away.

chapters.title: When the Cover Breaks
chapters.summary: Emrys broadcasts Kestrel's entire ledger—her own sanitized trails included—to every delegate, regulator, and newsroom as the port's failure begins, forcing the derivatives to trigger into a spotlight instead of shadow. Vale moves to kill her on the conference floor. POV: Emrys. Beat: climax—she chooses total exposure to save lives, burning her own cover as the weapon.

chapters.title: Aftermath in Daylight
chapters.summary: The tripwire freezes the payout; regulators swarm Halcyon; Ilya surrenders himself to testify, finally owning a name in public. Emrys refuses Halcyon's last offer of a new identity. POV: Emrys. Beat: cost and consequence—victory that doesn't undo the losses.

chapters.title: Emrys
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Emrys signs her own name to testimony before the commission, then shares a meal with Dara and Tomas in the reopened laundromat. Invisible no longer, she is still unfinished—but she belongs. POV: Emrys. Beat: resolution—identity as something built with others, not erased alone.
